name: Explicit Model Source-Authoring Provider Boundary
objective: Establish the first production-capable model-facing source-authoring provider behind the graduated GENERATE-001 implementation-content-generation contract, using an explicitly bounded transport and explicit caller-supplied credentials/configuration while preserving authoritative planning scope, repository immutability, downstream intent validation, and all existing approval and execution boundaries.
commitMessage: GENERATE-002: Build explicit model source-authoring provider boundary

generationContract.providerResponsibility: Construct a bounded source-authoring request from the exact GENERATE-001 provider input, invoke only the supplied model transport, and return candidate source content for the already-selected decision path.
generationContract.governanceResponsibility: GENERATE-001 remains solely responsible for choosing approved decisions, enforcing allowed and excluded paths, duplicate rejection, overwrite semantics, deterministic intent assembly, and final RiverDevImplementationIntent validation.
generationContract.transportResponsibility: Perform one explicitly requested model interaction from caller-supplied endpoint, model, credential, and request payload; return model response data without repository, Git, shell, approval, execution, commit, push, deployment, or scope authority.
generationContract.credentialBoundary: Credentials are supplied explicitly by the caller to the provider or transport configuration. GENERATE-002 must not search environment variables, dotenv files, repository secret files, or arbitrary credential stores.
generationContract.networkBoundary: Network access is permitted only inside the explicit model transport adapter. GENERATE core, planning, context, proposal, manifest, and execution governance remain non-networking.
generationContract.mutationBoundary: Provider and transport return in-memory candidate content only and perform no repository mutation.
generationContract.scopeBoundary: The model cannot select, add, replace, or broaden the target path. The exact target decision originates from the authoritative GENERATE-001 governance layer.
generationContract.approvalBoundary: Model output creates no proposal approval, implementation approval, execution authorization, commit authorization, push authorization, or deployment authorization.

acceptanceCriteria: A production model source-authoring provider implements the existing RiverDevImplementationContentGenerationProvider contract without changing its authoritative scope semantics.
The provider receives the exact plan, development context, and planning decision supplied by GENERATE-001 and cannot select a different target path.
The provider converts architecture-grounded context into a bounded model request sufficient to author candidate source content.
An explicit OpenAI-compatible transport boundary can perform the model interaction without introducing a model SDK dependency.
Endpoint, model identifier, credential, and transport are explicit configuration inputs rather than ambient secret discovery.
The provider never reads .env files, secret files, arbitrary environment credentials, or repository credentials.
Only the explicit transport adapter may perform network activity.
Provider and transport perform no repository write, Git mutation, shell execution, proposal approval, manifest generation, implementation, commit, push, or deployment.
Malformed, empty, structurally invalid, or unusable model responses fail closed before an implementation intent is returned.
Returned source content remains subject to the existing GENERATE-001 overwrite and implementation-intent validation boundaries.
Injected fake transport tests prove deterministic provider behavior without network access.
Existing GENERATE-001 tests and historical manually authored implementation intents remain compatible.
approvalBoundaries: No repository mutation authority may originate from model output.
No execution authority may originate from model output.
No proposal approval may originate from model output.
No commit or push authority may originate from model output.
No ambient credential discovery is authorized.
Live credential configuration and live model invocation remain a separate explicit operator-controlled boundary.
